title: Newcastle vs. Arsenal: Preview, Predictions, Talking Points
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackNov 20, 2026Arsenal are threatening to cruise to back-to-back titles. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Newcastle), Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty Images (Arsenal)Saturday’s Premier League action concludes on Tyneside, as the champions and league leaders Arsenal take on a Newcastle United team that’s still trying to find itself.

Matthias Jaissle’s impact was immediate after Eddie Howe’s departure, with Newcastle enjoying a five-game unbeaten run to open the season. However, Jaissle’s vertical and direct soccer has since failed to amuse, with the Magpies struggling for form entering the international break.
They’re toiling in a tightly packed mid-table, with the preseason fears that plenty of supporters aired coming to pass in the intervening period between the two international windows.

Arsenal are out to capitalize on the current consternation in the North East, heading into Saturday’s game five points clear at the summit. With their most likely competitors vulnerable, another win for the visitors would underline their intention to claim back-to-back titles at a canter.

Newcastle grew sick of the sight of David Moyes’s Everton before the break, with the Toffees knocking Jaissle’s side out of the Carabao Cup before claiming a 1–0 Premier League victory at St. James’ Park. Newcastle followed that dreary defeat up with a 1–1 draw at Fulham, a performance and result that the manager said was a “step in the right direction.”

While the hosts are certainly a work in progress, Arsenal are pretty much complete. Sure, there’s more for Arteta’s side to achieve, but this is a stable group that knows exactly what it takes to win in a tough environment on the road. The Gunners claimed their first victory at Anfield since 2012 earlier this month, and beat Hull City 1–0 before the break.

Arsenal have won their previous five Premier League outings. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesExpect the Toon Army to rise to the occasion as the champions come to town, with the two teams developing quite a bitter rivalry when Eddie Howe was at the helm.

Newcastle saw star man Bruno Guimarães join the Gunners in the summer, and although Arteta has suggested the home fans should welcome the Brazilian back on Saturday, there’s no chance that they will adhere to that advice.
This contest should have a bit of bite, suiting the hosts. The visitors won’t mind a bit of rough and tumble either, continuing to lean on their stout defense to allow their excellent run to persist.

Matthias Jaissle’s Newcastle have lost the most home games in the Premier League in 2026. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images• Arsenal’s form: The Gunners entered the previous international break reeling from a 3–0 defeat at Brighton, but they recovered tremendously in the aftermath. As a result, Arteta’s side are chasing a sixth successive league victory on Saturday and aiming to become just the fifth team in Premier League history to notch 10 wins from their opening 11 matches.

• Monkey off the Gunners’ backs: Arsenal used to dread trips to Tyneside when Howe was in charge, losing four of the previous five without scoring before they stole a 2–1 victory on Newcastle’s patch last season.

• Home discomforts: St. James’ Park was a horrible place to visit under Jaissle’s predecessor, but the fear factor that once emanated from Newcastle’s home turf has faded. No team has lost more Premier League home matches in 2026 than the Magpies (seven), and they’ve lost their previous two without scoring.
